precepts.text: Until we measure up unto the full stature of Christ.
precepts.point: If he die, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand men. And look what it says next. And if he live, he shall increase his name. So in other words, if you die, you better than a thousand men. And if you live, your name will continue growing. That's a man that's ever evolving, always getting better, until we measure up unto the full stature of Christ. You may understand that. Read.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Sirach describes the man who grows: “If he die, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand: and if he live, he shall increase it.” If you die, you leave a greater name than a thousand men, and if you live, your name keeps growing. That is a man who is ever evolving, always getting better, until we measure up unto the full stature of Christ. That measure is the goal the whole passage is climbing toward.

It comes in steps. First he serves “among great men” and appears “before princes”: studying four chapters a day, occupied in meditation and prophecies, keeping the sayings of the renowned men. Then he repents: he will “pray before the most High, and will open his mouth in prayer, and make supplication for his sins.” Then, “When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding”: when the Lord has seen you making a conscious change, mortifying and disciplining yourself. Before that, the strong meat is not for you. You have to learn the simple things first: no whoremonger shall enter the kingdom of heaven, wear your fringes, remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy, know the twelve tribes.

“In his secrets shall he meditate.” That is the transition from milk to meat. “He shall shew forth that which he hath learned”: out of his mouth comes the wisdom gathered over years of studying, applying, and getting around renowned men. “His name shall live from generation to generation.” That is what you want in your name, still part of the conversation after you leave this earth, for the wisdom God moved in you.

So you have to level up. As a teacher you cannot keep regurgitating the same classes over and over; you have to grow in understanding and application to teach the people. Growing to the full stature of Christ is how a name increases while you live.

precepts.text: Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them. That is what it means when it says we see through a glass darkly. We do not have the full understanding of all these scriptures.
precepts.point: For now we see through a glass, darkly. So what is the glass referring to?

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
The glass is the mirror, the unspotted image of the power of God. So why do we see it “darkly”? Ephesians answers: “Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them”.

That is what it means when it says we see through a glass darkly. We do not have the full understanding of all these scriptures. The understanding is darkened, and there is ignorance in us still.

Then go back to Corinthians: “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” When we are with Christ, he is going to make this clear to us. Until then no one should vaunt himself as if he knows it all.

So “And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.” Charity is the greatest because it is what keeps the body growing. People come in because they see how you move, how you conduct yourself and how you speak. You can teach all these scriptures with a photographic memory, but if you lack charity, if you are not kind and do not suffer long, the people will not stay.

precepts.text: Put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness. That is after the image of God: created in righteousness.
precepts.point: A lot of times people think the image and likeness is only about looking like God. We know from the scriptures and history that Christ and the apostles were of our people; but being after his image is more than the hue of your skin. Black and wicked is not the way to go; there are black devils too. It is the laws of God that make us special, not color alone.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
After his image and after his likeness means his spirit, the commandments of God. A lot of the time people think the image and likeness only means looking like God. Ephesians 4:24 shows what his image is: “put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”

That is after the image of God: created in righteousness. The man God made in his image was made to be righteous and holy, not only to share his color.

So being after his image is more than the hue of your skin. Black and wicked is not the way to go; you are still the devil. We say the white man is a devil, but there are black devils too. Just because you are black does not make you special unless you are righteous. It is the laws of God that make us special.

precepts.text: I did an interview with Soft White Underbelly. He said, when you're teaching this, doesn't it cause people to be angry? Yes, they get angry. The Bible says anger is okay: be ye angry, and sin not. The sin would be if you start murdering people; the sin would be you start stealing.
precepts.point: I met this one brother years ago at camp Eastern Parkway. He's on medication. He said, I would join you, but I have psychosis; I can't work, I get violent. I said, why? He says, I hate white people. He said, when I sit in the office or if I'm doing construction, I'll look at them and I just want to harm them.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
In an interview with Soft White Underbelly came the question: when you're teaching this, doesn't it cause people to be angry? Yes, they get angry. The Bible says anger is okay: “Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath”.

The sin would be if you start murdering people; the sin would be if you start stealing. Remember the series American Gods: Anansi was on a slave ship and asked, are you angry? That's good; anger gets stuff done. Surely oppression makes a wise man mad. Not I'm going to go kill everybody, but let's organize, let's do better. And you know who got that actor fired? Black people, who said what he was saying would make white people mad. The whole show was cancelled, and all those black people lost their jobs.

So “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother” does not mean you can't be angry at what was done. Be angry and sin not: let the anger drive you to organize and build, not to harm, steal or kill.

precepts.text: But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ. These men were not holding Christ as the head.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“And not holding the Head”: who is the Head? “But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ”. Christ is the head.

These men were not holding Christ as the head. They were putting Moses over Christ, animal sacrifice over the sacrifice of Christ.

Then Colossians 2:19 goes on: “from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered”. We are the body of Christ; we get our understanding, we are nourished through Christ. Follow what Christ said and we are going to be okay. “and knit together”, like we read in Judges 20 about being knit together as one man: honoring one another, preferring one another. “increaseth with the increase of God”: one man plants, another man waters, but it is God that gives the increase, and he is doing so.

So to hold the Head is to grow up into Christ in all things. Letting a man beguile you back to the ordinances is letting go of the Head the whole body is nourished from.

precepts.text: There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all. There are not different ways, different types, or different forms of God and how to worship God, no matter what Oprah said. There is only one way, one truth: keeping the commandments and faith in his son. That is what brought us together. If fellowship or friendships are what brought you here, you are in the wrong place. There is no separatism in the body of Christ; we are all one.
precepts.point: Video played from the grassroots: it was only three families. No garments, little three piece suits, unleavened bread, lamb, bitter herbs, wine, and music from the families. This is what longevity and endurance look like. At one point the bishops would serve all the people at Passover; changes had to happen because of expansion and growth, and those changes were not comfortable, but they were necessary to bring us to where we are today.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
“For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” A body has many parts that all work together: the heart that pumps blood, the brain that thinks, the arms and legs that move. We at Israel United in Christ are not many bodies. IUIC Austin, OKC, Atlanta and Arkansas are many members, but not different bodies. We are one body, in the same mind and the same spirit, so wherever you travel it should have the same feel and the same teachings.

Ephesians says it: “There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.”

There are not multiple ways, no matter what Oprah said. There are not different types or different forms of God and how to worship God. There is only one way, one truth, and to be in alignment with it you must do exactly what the body is supposed to do: keep the commandments and have faith in his Son.

That is what brought us together. If fellowship, friendships and relationships are what brought you here, you are in the wrong place. We are brothers and sisters who decided to do what God said against all odds and all the influences of the world; we don't care if you look at us funny.

We keep coming back to that soundness, that unity, that oneness in Christ. Anybody teaching anything other than that does not belong here. There is no separatism in the nation and no separatism in the body of Christ. We are all one.

precepts.text: He gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ. Though they had different offices and administrations, it was all for one goal. You see it in the teachers today: some focus on prophecy, some on organization and structure, some on marriage; each has his specialty, and you learn where to go glean from.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” The Lord is not the author of confusion; he is of order. When he brings in these different talents, gifts and members, he brings them for a purpose that serves one thing, with different functions. Paul shows it: “And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”.

All of it was for one goal: “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”. Though they had different offices and administrations, it was all for the perfecting of the saints.

You see it in the teachers today. Not all of them focus on the same things: some focus on prophecy, some on organization and structure, some on marriage, and you can see, that's his specialty. Learning from the deacons as the first internet member, you could see, he's good at this, I need some of that, and you learn where to go and what to glean.

What office can we say we don't need? If you think like that, you're not nation building; you haven't been given the vision. Back in the day some camps said, don't do anything with the videos, just play them. But the video needs music, an intro, something alluring, so someone outside the scriptures says, let me look at this, and once the scriptures start hitting: oh snap, I know who I am now. That effort is a member doing its part.

precepts.text: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: if we see a spirit here, as leaders we have to understand that spirit is elsewhere. But God is faithful, and will with the temptation also make a way to escape. What is the way to escape? Put a class on. Call a brother; speak to your brother, to get that spirit off of you. A lot of times the devil jumps on us and we start battling in our own mind and create a whole other reality that does not even exist. You talk to the brother and realize all that mess you were thinking and rehearsing is not even the case.
precepts.point: There is one body, and one Spirit: what is going on here is going on elsewhere. The Lord puts the spirit on the leadership to bring out the class that addresses the prevalent issue at the time. We are dealing with bitterness in the midst of Passover, and the Lord reveals it is not just here but throughout the congregations.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man.” Bitterness is a very common thing that many of us battle with. We are never alone in it: if leadership sees a spirit in one congregation, they have to understand that the same spirit is elsewhere. That is the “one body, and one Spirit” of Ephesians 4:4. The classes are not rehearsed, yet the same talking points come out in different places, because the Lord puts the spirit on the leadership to address the prevalent issue of the time, and in the midst of Passover He revealed bitterness throughout the congregations.

“But God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” Even while being tried and tempted, the Lord in His faithfulness makes a way out.

What is the way to escape? Put a class on. Call a brother. Speak to your brother, to get that spirit off of you. A lot of times the devil jumps on us and we start battling in our own mind, and we create a whole other reality that does not even exist in real life. You talk to the brother and you say, damn, all that mess I was thinking and rehearsing is not even the case.

That matters, because bitterness is the hidden leaven that must be purged. If it is not purged, it grows into a root that defiles the soul. Many brothers who left the body and came out with crazy videos started with a root of bitterness.

precepts.text: Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.
precepts.point: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you: you want to seek pardon from the Lord while you hold hatred toward your brother? We read what that gets.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Ephesians 4 says what to put away: “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” Bitterness comes first, and the rest come along with it: wrath, anger, clamour, and evil speaking, talking foolish and reckless about the brother, the sister, your wife. That thing has to be put away with extreme hatred. Instead: “be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.” You want to seek pardon from the Lord, but you have hatred toward your brother?

Colossians says what to put on in its place: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” That is how we have to move. The elect of God forbear and forgive one another.

Offenses are going to come in the congregation: a brother says something, a sister says something, and somebody gets offended. We all have to have mercy on one another, because we are all sick. This is a hospital. If a brother coughs on you, you forgive the brother, because everybody in here is sick.

This is how the bitter leaven gets purged. It came up in one congregation where a brother was bitter with his wife and it destroyed a household, and the same spirit showed up elsewhere. Left unchecked, it can destroy a congregation, so we put off the bitterness and put on mercy and forgiveness, as Christ forgave us.

precepts.text: Walk not as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind, alienated from the life of God through the blindness of their heart, given over unto lasciviousness. But ye have not so learned Christ.
precepts.point: Be ye followers of God as dear children, and walk in love. But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints. Paul wrote this way because that is what the Ephesians used to be caught up in.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
“Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children; And walk in love”. “But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints”. Why did Paul write to the Ephesians that way? Because that is what they used to be caught up in. Ephesus was a tough pagan environment. The worship of Diana, Artemis, involved all manner of lewd behaviour: they filled the great theatre, they had orgies, they got drunk, witchcraft, idolatry. Diana is the queen of heaven, the same as Ashtaroth, and the same as the Yoruba goddess, and our people were caught up in it in ancient times and today.

Chapter 4 shows it: “This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that ye henceforth walk not as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind, Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their heart”.

“Who being past feeling have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness. But ye have not so learned Christ”. Paul wrote in that form because he knew the lifestyle they came from, living as the Gentiles.

They were once “Gentiles in the flesh” and “aliens from the commonwealth of Israel”, but now made nigh by the blood of Christ, “fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God”: the northern kingdom, the so-called Argentinians, Colombians, Brazilians, Venezuelans, Puerto Ricans and Mexicans, the Israelites according to the Bible. So our people need to wake up and repent from the idolatry, the fornication and the lasciviousness, and flee from idolatry, or receive the same judgment coming on America.

precepts.text: Follow after charity and desire spiritual gifts.
precepts.point: Prophesying is for edification, exhortation and comfort, so gifts are for the body and not for oneself.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”. The Lord made some of us inside here apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors and teachers, and some brothers have several of these gifts. Why did God put his Holy Spirit in us and give us these gifts? Not so you can exalt yourself: I'm the mighty deacon, I understand all these things. It is “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry”. The gift is not for your own selfish reasons. It is to make the brothers better and the people perfect, and to help your people. You brothers travelling the world teaching the gospel are waking people up all over the world.

So Paul says “Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.” Desire spiritual gifts, but rather prophesy. Why? “But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.”

When you prophesy you teach and edify the people. You exhort the brothers to continue in the faith and to have hope; that is how brothers develop hope and faith, when the prophets among us go into the scriptures and show certain things. That feeling inside when you hear brothers teach who can prophesy is exhortation, and it revives you.

And it comforts, because we need that comfort. We are all going through certain things, and we are all tired of this world and this life. But when we go into the scriptures and see the things the Lord has prepared for us, it comforts us and exhorts us to continue in this gospel and this work. That is why the gifts are for the body and not for oneself.

precepts.text: Rooted and grounded in love, to comprehend with all saints.
precepts.point: Prophesying is for edification, exhortation and comfort, so gifts are for the body and not for oneself.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
The gifts are given “For the perfecting of the saints”, and prophecy gives edification, exhortation and comfort. Paul prays for the same: “That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love, May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height; And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge”.

With all the saints you have to comprehend the breadth, the width, the length, the depth and the height. It goes into what the Lord has prepared for those of us that love him. Once you fully understand that, it gives you hope, exhorts you and comforts you to continue in this walk and not fall out and go back into the world.

Some brothers and sisters have been with us for years and say, I can't take it no more, five years and I ain't got none, and they go back into the world and let Satan overcome them. If you want a husband or a wife, go to the Lord first: pray and fast, Lord, send me a righteous sister, send me a righteous husband. But get yourself right first, or it is not coming your way. Sisters want an Abraham but are not like Sarah; brothers want a Sarah while still living with mama.

“that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God. Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us, Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end.” That world without end is the church, a precept with Isaiah 45. Rooted and grounded in love, we comprehend what the Lord has for us and are filled with his fulness.

precepts.text: He that ascended descended first into the lower parts of the earth.
precepts.point: I have said ye are gods, but ye shall die like men.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
The children of the most High “walk on in darkness” and “die like men.” Ezra cries out over it: “it had been better not to have given the earth unto Adam: or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.” Adam ruled the heaven and the earth. Now we live in heaviness, the nations whooping our behind, and after death look for punishment. “O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.” Adam was not the only one kicked out of paradise. All his children fell with him.

That is why Christ came and died for our sins. Through one man sin came into the world, so through one man life came. He walked perfect and died for our sins, and he will choose which of us go back with him to paradise to rule the heaven and the earth: the ones who are real, who ask forgiveness, who keep fighting and never give up.

Paul's wording shows where we came from: “Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?” Christ ascended, but first he descended. His being born on the earth is called descending. The lower parts of the earth are here in captivity, the nether parts of the earth where his sons were cast out, and they descended the same way, by being born into the earth.

Even the fathers' names show it. Jared means descend, or descent: the sons of God came down to the nether parts of the earth and died, as Adam died. And Enoch, dedicated, trained, came down, trained himself to conquer the flesh, walked perfect, “and he was not; for God took him”: he went back up to paradise.

precepts.text: Let him that stole steal no more, but labour that he may give to him that needeth.
precepts.point: Biblical economics aims at communal wealth so that no generation is left stuck, and Israel should deal that way with each other now.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
“Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.” If you get blessed, it is to have to give to him that needeth. That is biblical, and that is part of the wisdom of Deuteronomy 4:6: the laws, statutes and commandments, everything written in the scripture, are our wisdom and our understanding, and we are to govern and deal with each other based on what God says.

How is that giving set up? You read it in Acts 2 and Acts 4: you put it at the feet of the leadership, and the leadership distributes as there is need. The leaders in the body initiate everything by the scripture, with the fundraising initiatives and the different offices, so that the body can be self-sustaining.

But many of us were raised in this environment and have not sharpened our senses, so we conduct business like Esau. Israelite businesses pop up, market to the body and make money off the body, and never come back and say, my pockets have gotten filled, my business has become profitable, I want to give back. Some even have cutthroat tactics, with no type of respect, moving the same way the world moves.

Those who say they are businessmen should read how the economics in Israel functioned and how we dealt with each other. Debt was forgiven every seven years so that debt would not pass from generation to generation. There was no usury, meaning no interest. Today what people wind up leaving behind is debt, and their families become responsible for it.

So the righteous way is to labour, prosper, and give back to the needy among our people. That is the foundation for seeing how Babylon, Esau and the rest of the world move in buying and selling, and why a nation that keeps God's statutes would be called “a wise and understanding people.”

precepts.text: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out.
precepts.point: Speak truth with your neighbour, let him that stole steal no more, and grieve not the Holy Spirit.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
“That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts”. The former conversation is the ways of this world, the love of this world. The old man, or old woman, is corrupt and filthy in the eyesight of the Lord, and that mentality manifests itself all the time. The ways of this world are deceitful lusts, hooks in your spirit that will take your soul out of the game. “And be renewed in the spirit of your mind”: by the scriptures. There must be change. That old man must be killed. If you are still the same three or four years in this truth, brothers and sisters, you need to really examine yourself; something is not right.

Acts shows the difference: “Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out”. First repent: you stop your sin, you stop breaking the laws of God. Then be converted, which is the actions behind that. You have to have a pattern of righteousness to follow, a pattern of good works, not dabbling in your old sin.

You used to lie; you used to steal. You are not doing those any more. But now what are you doing? You are speaking uprightly to your brothers. You are working, because now you need a manner of provision to provide not only for yourself and your family but for your nation that depends on you. That is the converted part: the works that follow repentance, showing that you truly repented and are no longer that old man or that old woman.

So “put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.” Put on the king that you are, and sisters, the attributes of your foremothers, the daughters of Sarah. Put away lying, “Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour”, and let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth. If you are not investing in the scriptures, the old man will come out in wickedness.

precepts.text: Be no more children tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men.
precepts.point: These ordinances belonged to the Levitical priesthood, and the doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office today do not even keep what they claim; they sound right because they use scriptures strongly and confidently, but they are in error. Be not tossed to and fro with every wind of doctrine, nor carried about with strange doctrines; do not ever fall away from the Messiah.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
The ram of consecration, the blood on the right ear, the thumb and the great toe, the wave offering and the heave offering that Aaron and his sons received “by a statute for ever from the children of Israel”: these ordinances belonged to the Levitical priesthood. You will read about the wave offering and the heave offering throughout the first five books, Leviticus predominantly.

The doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office today do not even keep what they claim. They sound right because they use scriptures strongly and confidently, but they are in error. “That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive”. Sleight of men and cunning craftiness is exactly how those doctrines are carried.

precepts.text: Be ye angry, and sin not; anger given room makes a man cast the commandments aside.
precepts.point: Moses is still good; he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount. He missed the promised land at that time, not the kingdom. But leadership carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath”. Anger itself is not the sin; but when anger takes hold, a man fails to apply what he knows. Moses knew the commandment: speak to the rock. In his anger at the people's disbelief he called them rebels and smote it twice. Anger lets the commandments slip.

That is how the Lord came to be angry with Moses for their sakes. Anger given room made him cast aside what the Lord had just told him, and he failed to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel. Be angry and sin not: the anger may come, but the commandment has to stay in hand.

precepts.text: The gifts are given for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ, till we all come into the unity of the faith unto a perfect man.
precepts.point: When he is able to congregate and be among his people, he blesses the Lord by keeping His laws, keeping His statutes, and going out declaring His glory to the children of Israel, showing them who they are, where they come from, and where they are going.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

precepts.why:
“My foot standeth in an even place: in the congregations will I bless the Lord.” The congregations are where the gifts are at work: “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ”.

The gifts are given for the perfecting of the saints, the work of the ministry and the edifying of the body of Christ, till we all come into the unity of the faith unto a perfect man. That is what keeps the foot standing in an even place, stable and steadfast in the truth.

When David is able to congregate and be among his people, he blesses the Lord by keeping His laws, keeping His statutes, and going out declaring His glory to the children of Israel, showing them who they are, where they come from, and where they are going.

precepts.text: That we henceforth be no more children tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men and cunning craftiness whereby they lie in wait to deceive.
precepts.point: When he is able to congregate and be among his people, he blesses the Lord by keeping His laws, keeping His statutes, and going out declaring His glory to the children of Israel, showing them who they are, where they come from, and where they are going.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

precepts.why:
His foot standing in an even place means he is stable and steadfast in his truth, not tossed to and fro: “That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive”.

There is no sleight of hand happening to him, no wind of doctrine throwing him around. The sleight of hand and cunning craftiness is the deception hitting our brothers and sisters: the sunrise sabbath, "you can eat whatever you want to." God is not about that. The foot stands even in the congregations, where the body of Christ is edified and not carried about.

precepts.text: Endeavoring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
precepts.point: When the spirit of the Most High comes upon you and you come into this truth, the many different skill sets we have come together to build up the house of the Lord, just like in the days of old. We are one body through the spirit.

note.label: Psalm 127: Except the Lord Build the House

precepts.why: “Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” We are one body through the spirit, and that unity is what holds the house together so that the Lord is the one building it and the labor is not in vain.

precepts.text: He gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers, till we all come unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.
precepts.point: The measuring line measures us up to the stature of Christ, the understanding of the laws and the doctrines.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
The man with the line measures a thousand cubits and the waters are to the ankles; a thousand more, to the knees; a thousand more, to the loins; then a river that cannot be passed over, “waters to swim in”. The rising water is the word being preached and the understanding increasing as it goes to the four corners of the earth: people coming to understand that Christ is a black man, that we are the Israelites, and that we must keep the commandments.

The measuring line measures us up to the stature of Christ. He “gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”. That measure is the understanding of the laws and the doctrines.

It comes in stages, ankles, knees, loins, just as understanding came out over time in the classes: the head covering out of First Corinthians 11, the sabbath, and the new moon being the full moon around 2006 to 2007. As long as we stay in the spirit, more revelation will keep coming, until the water is a river to swim in.

precepts.text: Be renewed in the spirit of your mind, put on the new man, and put away lying, speaking truth, for we are members one of another.
precepts.point: Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“And be renewed in the spirit of your mind; And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness. Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.”

To be renewed in the spirit of the mind is to be born again, to reboot the mind and clear out the programming of this world's philosophy. The new man puts away lying and speaks truth with his neighbour, because we are members one of another. Ananias did not put away lying as the renewed mind requires; the spirit upon him was covetousness as well as lying, for they saw the full value and coveted it.

precepts.text: Grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.
precepts.point: Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.”

Ananias lied to the Holy Ghost, and Peter tells him he has not lied unto men but unto God. Lying grieves the holy Spirit whereby we are sealed, which is why it is put away by the renewed mind.

precepts.text: Unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
precepts.point: The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.”

Not everyone has the same measure of grace. One man is put to death for a smaller sin while David was spared far greater ones, for grace is given by the measure of the gift of Christ. Ananias and Sapphira were given their measure, and great fear came upon all the church.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” Endeavor means by any means necessary. Do whatever it takes to keep unity. “There is one body, and one Spirit”. That one body is Christ. One spirit. “One Lord, one faith, one baptism”. One Lord, one faith, one baptism. “One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.”

“But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.” We might not serve the same purpose, but we come together perfectly bound under Christ. He's the only one who can bring the southern and northern kingdoms together. The Bible and Christ's spirit can bring a thousand black men and a thousand Hispanics together without one fight. No other book can do that.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 9 Explained Pt. 2

precepts.why: When the spirit of God says gather yourselves together, it means that; Paul said the same thing here. If you read this and then separate, you have the devil on you, you antichrist. “Endeavouring to keep the unity” What is that word? Unity. You are going to leave this gospel, leave the brothers and sisters that laboured with you? “of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” The bond of peace. “There is one body, and one Spirit,” One body, and one Spirit. So how are you going to separate, I'm going to do my own thing? You are not in the spirit of Christ; I don't know what Bible you are reading. “even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.” Those are the ones that have that singleness of mind, heart and soul, those that are about unity. When you separate from that spirit of unity, that spirit of Christ, you are not about unity; you are not about gathering the nation of Israel at all.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why: “And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.” That's the image. God created us to be righteous. Young men, God chose to make you after his likeness and gave you that spirit of righteousness. That's the message we must translate to the young ones.
